Title: Prabowo hits back at countries 'insulting' Indonesia over wildfire haze
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia's president railed Wednesday against "countries that like to insult" his nation over wildfires that have razed vast areas, spewing toxic haze into neighbouring countries.
The Southeast Asian giant has for months struggled to contain fires that Nusantara Atlas, an independent monitor analysing satellite data, said have consumed more than 1.9 million hectares in the nine months to September.
The haze has sent air pollution levels surging to dangerous levels not only at home, but also in Malaysia, Singapore and East Timor, prompting the Asean regional bloc to call a meeting over the crisis.
"As for certain countries that like to insult the Indonesian nation, when the time comes, we will reveal the companies involved" Prabowo told a cabinet meeting Wednesday, claiming that "many corporations bear responsibility" for the crisis.
He did not name names or nationalities.
The leaders of Indonesia's neighbours have offered help while steering clear of overt criticism at the highest diplomatic level.
With public anger growing, however, a Malaysian MP last week called for Indonesia to be treated as an "outcast" in the region.
"Indonesia is a polite and patient nation. Our country is often insulted, but believe me, our nation does not want to be insulted all the time," Prabowo said.
The president said he had asked for investigations into the cause of the fires which he insisted was "not purely natural."
Experts say Indonesia's wildfires can be blamed in large part on slash-and-burn land-clearing practices that result in the destruction of fire-resistant forest cover and drained peatlands.
This year, the blazes were intensified by a severe drought fuelled by the El Nino weather phenomenon.
"I am asking the police, the Attorney General's Office, the Ministry of Forestry, with the support of the Armed Forces and intelligence services, to investigate," said Prabowo.
"The people have also caught various individuals who deliberately set fires – this is something we can regard as environmental terrorism."
The president, who marked two years in office Tuesday with record-low approval levels, said deliberate fire-setting amounted to "a crime against humanity, because what they have done endangers the health of millions of our citizens."
Once the evidence is in, he added, "we will revoke all licenses of companies that violate the law."--AFP

Title: Indonesians sue government over wildfires, haze and public health crisis
Article:
PONTIANAK: Residents of Indonesian Borneo urged the government on Wednesday to do more to combat the wildfires consuming vast tracts of land and emitting a foul haze that has sickened thousands and curtailed daily life for months.
They spoke out as a court in Pontianak, West Kalimantan, began hearing arguments into the admissibility of a case brought against the state by residents in the province of nearly six million people.
"The issue... is not merely about burning forests and land, it is also closely tied to public health, air quality, economic activity, education and the safety of residents," resident Achmad Mundzirin told AFP in Pontianak.
"This lawsuit serves as a means to demand that the government be held accountable for its handling of forest and land fires," the 36-year-old said.
Lawyers have filed a class action case claiming "negligence, omission and failure" on the part of the government that has resulted in "a massive public health crisis" in West Kalimantan.
It singles out President Prabowo Subianto and 26 officials from the national, provincial and local government, as well as police and emergency services.
Glorio Sanen, a lawyer for the plaintiffs, told reporters on Wednesday the community was suffering.
"The president must directly lead the handling of this smoke disaster so that our aspirations, our hope for fresh air, blue skies and sunshine can return here in West Kalimantan," he said.
The government has deployed firefighters assisted by volunteers across affected areas, and used cloud-seeding and water-bombing with mixed success.
- 'ENVIRONMENTAL STRUGGLE' -
Experts say Indonesia's wildfires can be blamed in large part on slash-and-burn land-clearing practices that result in the destruction of fire-resistant forest cover and drained peatlands.
This year, the blazes have been intensified by a severe drought fuelled by the El Nino weather phenomenon.
The plaintiffs insist the government could have done more in preparation – drilling more borewells and distributing sufficient firefighting equipment.
They want the government to declare a national emergency to release resources and are suing for free health care and compensation for the families of people who died of fire-related respiratory ailments.
Rokman Torang, a lawyer for the state, insisted on Wednesday that the national and provincial governments "have already responded to this haze issue."
Prabowo said Wednesday that "many corporations bear responsibility" for the fire and haze crisis, and vowed a thorough investigation.
For Pontianak resident Andi Fachrizal, 54, the court case held "important meaning for the environmental struggle."
"This legal process is a moment to reaffirm that the public's right to a good and healthy environment is not merely a norm enshrined in laws and regulations, but a right that must be protected and fulfilled by the state," he told AFP.--AFP

Title: Police bust Geng Suria linked to 20 armed robberies in Kedah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have crippled an organised crime group known as Geng Suria, which was active in armed robberies across Kedah, following a special operation last month.
Federal Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M Kumar S Muthuvelu said the integrated operation, conducted in collaboration with the Kedah police contingent's Criminal Investigation Department, was carried out in Kedah and Perak from Sept 24 to 27.
He said the group was led by a 30-year-old man and had nine members aged between 28 and 52.
"The group has been active since early 2024. Geng Suria has been linked to 20 property and violent crime cases involving armed gang robberies that caused injuries in Kedah.
"Police arrested six suspects aged between 28 and 39. All are being detained under the Security Offences (Special Measures) Act 2012 (SOSMA) until Oct 25, 2026," he said in a statement today.
The remaining three members are being held at Sungai Buloh Prison, Pokok Sena Prison and Sungai Petani Prison over various other criminal offences, he said.
Elaborating on the group's modus operandi, M Kumar said Geng Suria often targeted foreigners' homes, business premises and residential properties identified by its leader.
"During the robberies, group members used dangerous weapons such as knives and machetes and did not hesitate to injure victims to carry out their criminal activities.
"Their aggressive and violent actions caused fear and trauma among victims, some of whom sustained serious injuries in the attacks," he said.
He said the stolen goods were subsequently sold, with the proceeds distributed by the group leader according to each member's role.
"During the raids, police seized six mobile phones of various brands and 189 ecstasy pills weighing an estimated 101.12g.
"The drug seizure is being investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952. Checks also found that several suspects had previous records involving vehicle theft, housebreaking, drugs and gang robbery," he said.
M Kumar said police reports received since 2024 indicated that Geng Suria's activities had caused losses amounting to hundreds of thousands of ringgit, while creating fear and threatening victims' safety.
He said the Attorney-General's Chambers had agreed to charge all nine alleged group members under Section 130V(1) of the Penal Code for being members of an organised criminal group.
"The 9 Geng Suria members will be charged tomorrow, Oct 22, 2026, at the Sungai Petani Sessions Court in Kedah," he said.

Title: Turkiye, Qatar, Pakistan, Indonesia sign defence cooperation accord
Article:
ANKARA: Turkiye, Qatar, Pakistan, and Indonesia signed an agreement on Wednesday to boost defence cooperation and strengthen defensive capabilities, the Turkish Defence Ministry said.
In a statement, the ministry said the countries signed the "Badr Memorandum of Understanding" in Doha as a sign of their desire to further deepen cooperation and develop partnerships.
"The agreement holds substantial economic importance," it said, adding the accord sought to foster cooperation in military production, boost military capabilities, and help collaboration in technical military training, research and development.
"By leveraging the unique military production capabilities of each country, the initiative will facilitate cooperation and integration, enhance defence industrial capacities, and enable the fulfillment of the needs of allied and friendly nations," it added.
Turkiye, which has Nato's second-largest army and a robust defence industry, has been helping Gulf nations, including Qatar, where it has a military base, bolster their defences amid the Iran war.
In August, it signed a mutual defence pact with nuclear-armed Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, under which an attack on one party constitutes an attack on all. Ankara also has close ties with Indonesia, notably in the defence industry.
The ministry said the Badr accord would strengthen ties between the countries' defence industries and bolster collaboration to promote security and achieve shared objectives.
Haluk Gorgun, the chairman of Turkiye's Defence Industry Presidency, said the accord formed the foundation of a "strategic cooperation" to develop joint production and technology.
"Technology sharing, joint development and strengthening domestic production capabilities lie at the heart of sustainable defence industry. As Turkiye, we value partnerships that go beyond off-the-shelf procurement models, that foster the development of a nation's own human capital and industrial infrastructure," Gorgun said in a statement.
"We believe that the Badr Memorandum of Understanding will contribute to transforming the complementary capabilities of Qatar, Pakistan, Indonesia, and Turkiye into concrete projects," he added.--REUTERS

Title: Viral school fight video shows June incident classified NFA
Article:
BENTONG: A viral video showing a fight involving students and adults outside a school here depicts an incident in June that police have classified as no further action (NFA).
Acting Bentong police chief Deputy Superintendent Azmi Mahmod said the 31-second video resurfaced on Facebook yesterday.
"The incident occurred on June 16 after the victim's father lodged a police report alleging that his son had been assaulted and threatened by two youths in front of a school.
"Police arrested two boys, aged 15 and 16, on the same day. They were remanded for two days before being released on police bail on June 18," he said in a statement today.
Azmi said the suspects were investigated under Section 323 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt and Section 506 for criminal intimidation.
He said the investigation papers were resubmitted to the deputy public prosecutor on July 15, after which the case was classified as NFA following consideration of developments in the investigation, including the complainant's decision to withdraw the report and not pursue the case.
"Police conducted the investigation transparently, in accordance with established procedures and applicable laws. We take incidents involving the safety and welfare of school students seriously.
"We urge the public not to spread unverified information or make statements about the video that could cause confusion," he said.

Title: IRDA appoints Ashari Kasnan as chief executive, effective Nov 1
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Iskandar Regional Development Authority (IRDA) has announced the appointment of Datuk Ashari Kasnan as its chief executive, effective Nov 1, 2026, succeeding Datuk Mohd Noorazam Osman who has served since Jan 1, 2025.
In a statement today, IRDA said this appointment marks a new chapter in IRDA's leadership as Iskandar Malaysia builds on two decades of regional development and advances its next phase of growth.
"Ashari's appointment comes as Iskandar Malaysia moves beyond its 20th anniversary in 2026 and enters its next phase of regional development.
"As chief executive, he will lead IRDA's efforts to facilitate strategic investments, strengthen the region's economic competitiveness and promote balanced, inclusive and sustainable growth, while advancing Iskandar Malaysia's long-term development priorities and reinforcing Johor's position as a competitive investment destination," IRDA said.
Ashari has more than three decades of experience in the Johor state civil service, with a career spanning land administration, district administration, institutional development, entrepreneurship and economic development.
Prior to his appointment at IRDA, he served as the chief executive officer of the Johor State Biotechnology and Biodiversity Corporation (J'Biotech) and J-Biotech Holdings Sdn Bhd.
His previous appointments include deputy state secretary of Johor (development), director of the Johor Land and Mines Office, Mersing district officer, and executive director and general manager of Perbadanan Usahawan Johor Sdn. Bhd. (PUJB).

Title: Encorp wins Felda job to build staff housing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Encorp Bhd's subsidiary Encorp Construction & Engineering Sdn Bhd has secured a RM16.96 million contract to build staff housing for its major shareholder Federal Land Development Authority (Felda).
The contract follows a memorandum of understanding signed on June 5 this year.
"The parties are currently in the process of finalising the definitive agreement in relation to the project.
"The company will make further announcements on any material developments in relation to the above, as and when necessary," Encorp said in a filing to Bursa Malaysia.
Felda, through Felda Investment Corp Sdn Bhd, holds a 67.13 per cent stake in Encorp.
Encorp's shares closed unchanged at 16 sen today, giving the company a market capitalisation of RM50.7 million.

Title: 10-month-old boy died from 'blunt force' head injuries
Article:
BUTTERWORTH: A 10-month-old boy who was found weak at his babysitter's home died from head injuries consistent with blunt force trauma, police said
Seberang Prai Utara district police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuar Abdul Rahman said doctors could not determine whether the injuries were caused by an accident or another person's actions.
"The medical findings could not establish the number of impacts, the object used or the exact time the injuries occurred.
"The medical findings showed that the victim died from head injuries consistent with blunt force trauma. Doctors also confirmed that the injuries could have been fatal," he said when contacted.
The baby was reportedly in good health when his mother sent him to the babysitter's home at about 5.40am on Monday.
He was later found weak. The babysitter sought her husband's help to perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) before the baby was taken to Sungai Dua Health Clinic for further treatment.
However, the baby was believed to have died before reaching the clinic.
The babysitter was remanded for a week yesterday to assist in the investigation.

Title: eBay to lay off 9pct of workforce in push to simplify operations, internal memo shows
Article:
EBay will lay off about nine per cent of its workforce as the online marketplace looks to simplify operations and shift resources to its fastest-growing areas, CEO Jamie Iannone told staff in a memo that was reviewed by Reuters.
A spokesperson for eBay confirmed the layoffs to Reuters on Wednesday.
The move will eliminate around 1,100 jobs, based on the 12,300 employees eBay had at the end of last year. The company also let go about six per cent of its workforce, or 800 employees, in February as part of efforts to streamline operations.
EBay has set itself apart from rivals by pushing into authenticated luxury goods, collectibles and refurbished products, which draw enthusiasts willing to pay more for valuable items. That has helped its shares rise nearly 40 per cent this year, outperforming the benchmark S&P 500's around 12 per cent gain.
"Our strategy is working," Iannone said in the memo, adding that "continuing to capture the significant opportunity ahead requires us to make thoughtful choices about where we focus and invest."
He said affected staff would be informed in the coming days.
Shares of eBay were down 1.8 per cent in premarket trading.
The company has this year also benefited from its US$1.4 billion deal for ​fashion resale platform Depop, which expanded its reach among younger consumers ​and strengthened its position in the growing re-commerce market.
That helped eBay forecast third-quarter revenue above Wall Street estimates when it last posted results, in August. The company is slated to report latest earnings next week.
Those efforts have also caught the eye of GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen, who made an unsolicited US$56 billion bid for the much larger eBay in May.
EBay had rejected the offer, saying that it was "neither credible nor attractive."

Title: Speaker awaits clarification on PN deregistration
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The status and position of Perikatan Nasional (PN) MPs in the opposition bloc will be determined after parliament receives clarification on the coalition's deregistration.
Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said a decision could not be finalised pending clarification from PN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar.
He was responding after Mohd Sany Hamzan (PH-Hulu Langat) raised the issue while Kamal Ashaari (PN-Kuala Krau) was debating in the Dewan Rakyat.
"There is no ruling on the status and position of PN MPs in the Dewan Rakyat. I have also written to the PN chairman (Ahmad Samsuri).
"God willing, once I receive clarification from the chairman, I will inform the House," he said.
Yesterday, the Registrar of Societies Malaysia (RoS)
confirmed that it had cancelled PN's registration
, saying the coalition's explanation failed to address the grounds for cancellation outlined in an earlier notice.
RoS said the decision was made under subparagraph 13(1)(c)(iv) of the Societies Act 1966 (Act 832), after reviewing the documents and representations submitted by PN on Oct 12.
It said an earlier notice dated Sept 22 had been issued to PN under subsection 13(2) of the Act, giving the coalition 30 days to explain why its registration should not be cancelled.
Pas criticised the deregistration, which came two days before the High Court was scheduled to hear PN's legal challenge against the restrictions.
Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said the timing raised questions, particularly as the hearing on PN's application for a stay of the suspension order was scheduled for Oct 22.
He claimed the move reflected the Madani government's fear of PN, particularly ahead of the Melaka election and the next general election.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ditch Waze, NSC tells Malaysians
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The National Security Council (NSC) has called on civil servants and Malaysians to switch from navigation application Waze to locally developed alternatives, saying security risks involving Israel cannot be compromised.
The call follows Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's directive for civil servants
to stop using Waze
and his appeal for the public to do the same, citing concerns that sensitive government information and personal data could be exploited by Israel.
The NSC said the government took seriously the collection of users' location data, movement patterns, travel information and device details by Waze.
"The government takes seriously the collection of users' location data, movement patterns, travel information and device details by navigation application Waze, particularly as its Terms of Use provide for the application of Israeli law and the jurisdiction of Israeli regime courts in disputes relating to the use of its services.
"There can be no compromise on any security risks involving Israel. The protection of Malaysians' data and the sovereignty of the country's information must always be prioritised, including when assessing the implications of using applications subject to foreign laws and jurisdictions," it said in a statement.
The council called on civil servants and the public to use local navigation applications such as TuJu, developed by the Malaysian Highway Authority (MHA), or other suitable locally developed alternatives.
The National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa) and the NSC have also prepared a frequently asked questions document on the matter, available at https://www.nacsa.gov.my/faq-waze.php.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sarawak civil servants to receive two months' salary in special aid
Article:
KUCHING: Sarawak will pay state civil servants special financial assistance equivalent to two months' salary in recognition of their contributions to the state's development.
Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Abang Openg said the assistance would be based on their last-drawn basic salaries for November 2026 and paid before the end of this year.
He said the payment was expected to benefit about 19,851 state civil servants, with an allocation of RM144 million.
"I am pleased, on behalf of the cabinet and Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS), to announce special financial assistance equivalent to two months' salary for members of the Sarawak State Public Service," he said when delivering his winding-up speech at the Sarawak Legislative Assembly sitting.
The state government also announced a one-off payment of RM700 for federal civil servants serving in Sarawak.
Abang Johari said the assistance was in recognition of the service and sacrifices of federal personnel, including teachers, healthcare workers and security personnel, who also contributed to the state's development.
The payment is expected to benefit about 132,347 federal civil servants, with an estimated allocation of RM93 million. It will be disbursed in the first quarter of 2027.
The state government also announced a one-off payment of RM500 for each retired member of the Sarawak State Public Service.
Abang Johari said the payment was expected to benefit about 10,141 retirees, with an allocation of RM51 million, in recognition of their contributions during their service.
The GPS government also announced a one-off incentive of RM700 for each private media practitioner registered with six media associations in Sarawak, in recognition of their role in delivering information and news professionally.
Abang Johari said the state's development depended on the hard work of civil servants in implementing various projects, including bridges, clean water and electricity supplies, and infrastructure connecting rural communities.
He said an efficient, transparent and accountable public service was essential to achieving the Post-Covid-19 Development Strategy 2030 and strengthening Sarawak's efforts to claim its rights under the Malaysia Agreement 1963.
He said the state government would continue to safeguard civil servants' welfare by building and upgrading government offices and quarters, including in remote areas, while investing in leadership development and capacity building.
He urged Sarawakians to preserve peace and unity and not allow external elements to divide the state.
"Instead, remain united in defending Sarawak's rights and future to achieve the Sarawak Maju Makmur agenda," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Macron takes aim at Trump for using France riots for election gain
Article:
PARIS: President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday took an apparent swipe at counterpart Donald Trump of exploiting France's riots for advantage in the US midterm election battle, as Paris prepared for more protests this weekend.
Macron, speaking during a visit to Qatar, implied that Trump, and possibly Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is also in election mode, made "stupid comments" on the unrest for political gain, though he did not name either leader.
"There are people who campaign at France's expense – leaders who are in campaign mode, whether here in the region or on the other side of the Atlantic," he told reporters in Doha.
Macron made his remarks as he and his government struggled to get on top of a crisis that has scarred France's image both abroad and in financial markets, six months ahead of presidential elections to choose his successor.
France's government has admitted it "lost control" in the frenzy of street violence that erupted last weekend, when masked youths clashed with police, looted shops and vandalised public buildings.
Trump has sought to link the "revolution" in France to "migrants, jihadists, and communists" as he campaigned for his Republican party in the United States on his anti-immigration messaging.
He also on Tuesday hailed French far-right leader Marine Le Pen, who shares his ideologies, as a conservative voice, with surveys putting her as the frontrunner in France's presidential race.
Trump's ally Netanyahu, facing his own tough election battle, on Tuesday argued that France had been hit by an "invasion."
Several analysts have dismissed the claims that migrants were driving France's protests.
- CURFEWS -
The unrest overshadowed demonstrations held Saturday in which more than half a million people marched nationwide against the cost of living. Those rallies followed four weeks of student protests that have closed many schools across France.
Since the rioting – the worst France has seen in years – and ahead of further cost-of-living demonstrations this coming Saturday, Macron's government has warned it will brook no further violence.
Authorities in Paris and several other cities imposed nighttime curfews Monday and Tuesday in certain zones prone to protests or looting.
Macron said that on Thursday he would chair a meeting of key ministers and intelligence officials to receive a "detailed account" of what happened last weekend.
French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu, who on Wednesday held a meeting with union leaders organising marches, has vowed a "massive" police deployment for the fresh demonstrations called for Saturday by the Yellow Vest movement protesting rising inflation.
The convulsion in France, the EU's second-biggest economy after Germany, has rattled financial markets already nervous about the country's growing debt pile and deficit.
The yield on the French government's benchmark 10-year bond has been rising, and on Wednesday surpassed five percent as investors demanded a higher return given the fiscal woes. A rising yield signifies a drop in bond prices. The Paris stock market also fell.
On Friday, the Moody's ratings agency is expected to lower its grade on France's public debt.
The country's political landscape is so fragmented that Lecornu has little chance of winning swift parliamentary consensus for a cost-cutting budget that needs to be adopted before the end of this year.
- LE PEN LEADS RACE -
The latest survey, carried out by Ifop in the wake of the riots, suggested Le Pen would lead first-round voting intentions by a wide margin and far-left candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon emerged as her most likely opponent in the runoff.
France's neighbours Italy and Belgium have also started to experience similar unrest, on a smaller scale. Italy's government has ordered 500 troops to Milan to stem street violence there.
Macron said that "we don't need a state of emergency" that would likewise permit soldiers to reinforce police against rioters, adding that "we have the means" already at authorities' disposal, such as curfews.
While the partial curfews have led to a calming of the situation in Paris and elsewhere, they have disrupted travel for commuters looking to take urban rail after 11pm (2100 GMT).
"It's quite disconcerting," said one Paris commuter who gave only his first name, Louis, when he found his line closed. But "if it can prevent further acts of vandalism... then yes, I think it's a good thing", he said.
The Yellow Vest movement behind last weekend's demonstrations announced Wednesday it had formally told authorities it planned to hold its Paris march on Saturday starting from Bastille square.
The movement also wants to hold follow-up nationwide demonstrations on Nov 5.
The images broadcast around the world of France's street violence last weekend have prompted several countries, including the United States, China and Germany, to issue travel advisories for their citizens in France.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malakoff names Aznita Abdul Aziz as director, Nurshazwani Abd Malek as covering CFO
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malakoff Corp Bhd has appointed Aznita Abdul Aziz as an independent non-executive director effective today.
Aznita brings about 26 years of experience in the oil and gas industry, primarily with the Petronas group, covering risk management, strategic planning, portfolio management, treasury operations and economic evaluation.
She is currently an independent non-executive director of Steel Hawk Bhd, where she chairs the nomination committee and sits on the audit and risk management committee and the remuneration committee.
Separately, Malakoff appointed deputy chief financial officer Nurshazwani Abd Malek as covering chief financial officer from Dec 1.
She will assume the role on an interim basis following the departure of Mohd Nazersham Mansor, who steps down on Nov 30 to pursue other career opportunities.
Malakoff chairman Tan Sri Wan Zulkiflee Wan Ariffin said Aznita's experience in risk management, strategic planning and portfolio management would be valuable to the board, given her 26-year career in the oil and gas industry.
"Her perspective and expertise will be a strong addition to our board as we continue to navigate the opportunities and responsibilities that come with being Malaysia's largest independent power producer.
"On behalf of the board, I also wish to place on record our sincere appreciation to Mohd Nazersham for his years of service and the contributions he has made to Malakoff.
"We wish him the very best in his future endeavours," he said in a statement.
As Malaysia's largest independent power producer, the group continues to pursue its ambitions across power generation, renewable energy and environmental services, with strong leadership and sound governance at its core.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Eonmetall shares to be suspended from Nov 4 ahead of delisting
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Trading of Eonmetall Group Bhd (EGB) shares on the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia will be suspended with effect from 9am on Wednesday, Nov 4, 2026.
Eonmetall said the trading of EGB shares will continue to be suspended until the delisting of EGB from the official list of Bursa Malaysia following the completion of the selective capital reduction (SCR).
"Accordingly, the last day and time for trading of EGB shares on the Main Market prior to the suspension will be at 5 pm on Tuesday, Nov 3, 2026," it said.
It said that under the SCR, all shareholders of EGB, other than Eonmetall Corporation Sdn Bhd and Datuk Goh Cheng Huat, whose names appear on the record of depositors and/or register of members of EGB as at 5pm on Thursday, Nov 5, 2026, shall be entitled to receive cash consideration.
The cash consideration is RM0.45 for each EGB share held on the entitlement date.
"The capital repayment will be made within 10 days from the entitlement date," it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MPs call for stronger school safety measures after Kuching attack
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Incidents involving the safety of students and teachers should no longer be treated as isolated cases, given their repeated occurrence in recent years, said Dr Kelvin Yii Lee Wuen (PH-Bandar Kuching).
He said the
latest incident involving
a student at an international school in Kuching had heightened concerns among parents and students about school safety.
Yii said the issue should not be viewed solely as a criminal matter, but also as an education and mental health concern requiring a comprehensive response, when debating the Supply Bill 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.
The teacher was reported to have been injured and taken to hospital.
Yii cautioned that school violence could potentially inspire copycat behaviour, particularly when students were exposed to reports of similar cases and negative influences on social media and through gaming.
"I do not want schools to become places where metal detectors have to be installed at their main entrances.
"That is not the image I want to see, but if it is necessary, we must ensure our children's safety is prioritised," he said.
Two other members of parliament (MPs) raised similar concerns over school safety, bullying and violence.
Hassan Saad (PAS-Baling) asked whether enough was being done to protect students from bullying, intimidation and violence.
"Parents send their children to school in the morning hoping they will return home safely.
"But what if their children live in fear every day because they are harassed, threatened or bullied by their own peers?" he said.
Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin (Bersatu-Masjid Tanah) said more teachers should be equipped with psychological knowledge to help identify students with behavioural problems.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Oil prices jump US$2 as Iran dents hopes of diplomatic progress
Article:
LONDON: Oil prices jumped more than US$2 on Wednesday after Iran said there was little reason to expect diplomatic progress with the United States, leaving Brent crude near five-month highs, with further support from falling US crude and fuel inventories.
Brent crude futures gained US$2.06, or 1.9 per cent, to US$110.85 a barrel by 1048 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose US$2.13, or 2.2 per cent, to US$99.95.
In the previous session, Brent hit its highest level in five months, while WTI touched a six-month peak before prices fell following discussions on mediation efforts during a meeting between Iran's president and Pakistan's army chief in Tehran.
On Wednesday, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi told the Financial Times that Iran was fully prepared to defend itself, while President Masoud Pezeshkian told state media that the United States could not expect dialogue while blockading and threatening Iran.
"Neither of the two geopolitical conflicts underpinning the market's bullish sentiment has shown any signs of de-escalation," PVM analysts said, referring to the Middle East and Russia-Ukraine wars.
At least 18 vessel attacks were recorded over the past two weeks, Kpler data showed, while LSEG analysts said Iran was targeting tankers well beyond the Strait of Hormuz, extending into the Gulf of Oman and threatening Gulf crude loadings and ship-to-ship transfers supporting regional shipments.
Iran-aligned Houthis on Monday claimed responsibility for attacks on a Saudi Aramco site in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield and airports in Riyadh and Abha, Saudi Arabia.
In the United States, two Energy Department officials said on Tuesday that they were working with refiners worldwide to boost fuel output.
US crude stocks fell by 4.9 million barrels in the week ended October 16, with gasoline and distillate inventories also declining, market sources said, citing American Petroleum Institute data.

Title: Prabowo accuses MSCI of trying to intimidate Indonesia after market rout
Article:
JAKARTA: Global index provider MSCI was trying to "intimidate" Indonesia, but the country would not be afraid, President Prabowo Subianto told his Cabinet on Wednesday in his first public response to last week's downgrade warning.
MSCI stepped up pressure on Jakarta by announcing that it could downgrade Indonesia's equities to "standalone" market status, saying the country had not done enough to crack down on coordinated trading practices in its stock market.
The surprise announcement triggered a record two-day stock market rout, with a downgrade threatening to cause massive capital flight and cut the US$1.5 trillion G20 economy off from major emerging market index flows.
"The MSCI... intended to intimidate us," Prabowo told a gathering of his Cabinet in a speech broadcast on the government's official YouTube channel.
"I simply say to MSCI: the Indonesian nation fears no one and will not be cowed," he said, adding that the country possessed strength and courage, was willing to make sacrifices and refused to surrender.
In an emailed response to a request for comment, MSCI said its decisions followed transparent and rules-based methodologies.
"MSCI will continue to monitor developments in the Indonesian market and engage with market participants and authorities," it said.
Prabowo, a former special forces commander, has often used strongly nationalist language since coming to power in 2024, suggesting that foreign powers were determined to destabilise Indonesia, the world's largest Muslim-majority country and a global commodities powerhouse.
His speech on Wednesday also referred to outside interference in Indonesia, although he did not elaborate.
Other senior Indonesian political figures have also reacted strongly to MSCI's warning.
On Tuesday, former Indonesian trade minister M. Lutfi claimed on his Instagram account that Singapore sovereign wealth funds Temasek and GIC were involved in pressuring MSCI to issue the warning to Indonesia.
An official from Temasek described Lutfi's comments as "patently untrue", while GIC also rejected the allegation, DealStreet Asia reported on Wednesday.
Last week, senior economic minister Airlangga Hartarto also said there was "a big question mark" over why MSCI had not discussed the possible downgrade during meetings with Indonesian officials in Bangkok just days earlier.
Hanif Dhakiri of the National Awakening Party, who sits on the parliamentary committee overseeing finance affairs, called for MSCI's methodology to be transparent, objective and consistently applied across countries.
"We should not be defensive in the face of criticism, but neither should we accept judgements without examining their basis and objectivity," he told Reuters.
Said Abdullah, a lawmaker from the opposition PDI-P party, said on Sunday that Indonesia should take MSCI's concerns seriously, but argued that the index provider's judgements should not be beyond scrutiny.
"MSCI's executives are not prophets delivering divine revelations, like apostles writing sacred texts, who can claim a monopoly on flawless truth," he said.

Title: Kelantan police enlist community leaders in fight against drugs
Article:
RANTAU PANJANG: Kelantan police will enlist community leaders and members of the public to strengthen efforts to combat drug abuse and trafficking in the state.
Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said police welcomed information and cooperation from the public to support ongoing efforts to tackle the drug problem.
He said the force would reach out to community leaders and individuals to encourage them to play an active role in helping the authorities combat drug-related activities.
"The police also welcome any information from the public that can assist our efforts," he said.
Yusoff said Kelantan police declared war on drugs in 2024 to instil a stronger commitment among personnel to combat the problem.
He cited a recent incident in Kampung Lalang Pepuyuh, Tanah Merah, in which a narcotics policeman confronted a man suspected of being a drug addict, as an example of the commitment required in the fight against drugs.
He said police personnel were prepared to face significant risks, including serious injuries, while carrying out their duties to curb drug-related activities.
Yusoff said drug-related offenders could commit various crimes, including violence against family members, while drug abuse could also lead to property crimes.
"Drug abuse is the root cause of many problems. Drug-related criminals can do anything, including harming their own parents or wives, let alone committing property crimes.
"That is why we will continue to focus on combating drugs and make this effort a priority," he said.
He stressed that police would remain committed to tackling the drug problem, adding that public cooperation and information were crucial to strengthening enforcement efforts and protecting the community.
Earlier, Yusoff, accompanied by Kelantan deputy police chief Datuk Mohd Ali Thamby and Kelantan Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Dr Douglas Nyeging Taong, visited the injured 37-year-old corporal at his home here today.

Title: MAHB to deploy K9 units at KLIA from Oct 26 amid heightened drug smuggling scrutiny
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd will deploy K9 patrol units inside the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) terminals on Oct 26, amid heightened scrutiny over recent transnational drug smuggling cases originating from the airport.
Managing Director Datuk Mohd Izani Ghani said the deployment will cover passenger-facing areas such as the departure hall, arrival hall and customs inspection areas, enabling early detection of prohibited items and potential security threats linked to targeted flights.
He said the canine units will also be extended to baggage handling and sorting areas to reinforce checks on checked-in luggage before it is loaded onto aircraft or transferred to reclaim carousels.
"This layered security approach aims to strengthen coverage across passenger-facing and back-of-house areas, complementing existing security arrangements," he said in a statement today.
Izani said a pilot phase will be conducted to assess the effectiveness of the selected locations and identify any necessary adjustments to passenger flows and deployment schedules.
He said that KLIA will coordinate with relevant agencies on operational matters, including standard operating procedures, designated access for K9 units and handlers, and support facilities within the terminals.
"This collaboration also allows our Aviation Security personnel to remain focused on their core responsibility of safeguarding airport users and facilities.
"We will continue to support the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency, the police, Customs Department and the K9 units in ensuring that KLIA remains a safe, comfortable and clean airport for everyone," he said.
Earlier, KLIA police chief ACP M. Ravi said police had stepped up K9 patrols, previously conducted periodically, to bolster airport security following several recent incidents.
The tighter measures follow public scrutiny of screening protocols at the country's main international gateway after several Malaysians were intercepted overseas carrying illicit drugs.
On Oct 10, five Malaysians — two men and three women aged between 19 and 26 — were arrested by Japanese customs officers at Tokyo's Haneda Airport after about 5kg of cocaine worth 120 million yen (RM3.1 million) was found hidden in the hollowed-out insoles of their shoes.

Bukit Aman confirmed the group had departed from KLIA Terminal 2 and were allegedly acting as drug mules paid RM8,000 each.
The case followed another high-profile incident in July, when Indonesian authorities arrested a 39-year-old Malaysian commercial airline pilot upon arrival at Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport after uncovering more than 70,000 ecstasy pills weighing about 26kg and a packet of methamphetamine in his luggage.
Adding urgency to the tightened airport measures, Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan revealed yesterday that international drug syndicates were shifting tactics to evade airport detection.
He said their methods include last-minute flight bookings for drug mules and deliberately scheduling flights during peak hours at KLIA to exploit heavy passenger congestion.

Title: Pantech Global's Q2 earnings soar 90pct
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pantech Global Bhd's net profit soared 89.5 per cent to RM19.33 million in the second quarter ended Aug 31, 2026 (Q2 FY27), from RM10.2 million a year earlier.
The steel pipe and fittings manufacturer said this was supported by higher selling prices, a more favourable product mix and improved operating leverage, which helped offset the impact of tariffs and rising raw material and energy costs.
Pantech's quarterly revenue increased 36.9 per cent to RM173.71 million from RM126.9 million a year earlier, driven by higher sales volume and improved average selling prices.
Its earnings per share rose to 2.27 sen from 1.20 sen a year earlier.
For the first half of FY27, Pantech's net profit increased 60.6 per cent to RM35.69 million from RM22.23 million a year earlier, while revenue rose 32 per cent to RM333.39 million from RM252.53 million.
The company annpunced a first interim single-tier dividend of 2.2 sen per share for FY27, payable on Dec 16 this year.
Pantech group managing director Adrian Tan said its first half performance reflected the resilience of the business and its continued focus on balancing sales growth with profitability.
"Higher sales volumes and improved average selling prices, together with a more favourable product mix and greater operating efficiency, supported stronger earnings despite the ongoing pressures from rising input costs," he said in a statement.
Tan said the company remains focused on sustaining its business momentum in the second half of FY27.
"We expect performance in the second half to be stronger than in the first half, supported by resilient demand across our key end-user industries and continued attention to pricing discipline, cost management and operational efficiency.
"At the same time, we remain mindful of uncertainties surrounding geopolitical developments, trade policies and raw material prices, which could affect market demand and margins," he said.

Title: Locals swoop in to shield foreign operators in Klang business crackdown
Article:
KLANG: Several Malaysians turned up claiming to be employers or caretakers of business premises during an immigration crackdown on businesses suspected of being operated by or employing foreigners in Meru here today.
The situation unfolded at several premises inspected during a joint operation by the Selangor Immigration Department and Klang Royal City Council (MBDK), which began at 11am.
The operation targeted various businesses, including barber shops, vehicle workshops, grocery stores, car washes and mobile phone shops.
At one premises, a Bangladeshi man believed to be the employer became agitated when MBDK enforcement officers inspected his shop.
The man, who was accompanied by his Malaysian wife, refused to identify his foreign workers and gave various excuses when questioned by enforcement personnel.
A local man later arrived, claiming to be the brother of the Bangladeshi man's wife and introducing himself as the caretaker of the premises.
"I don't know who is working today. I just returned from the clinic after taking my child there," the Bangladeshi man told enforcement officers.
However, when officers asked him to review the premises' closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage, he fell silent and refused to cooperate.
At another premises, a mobile phone shop suspected of employing foreigners, a Malaysian woman arrived during the inspection and claimed to be its caretaker.
Similar situations were observed at several other businesses, where foreign workers detained by enforcement officers claimed their employers were Malaysians, apparently in an attempt to avoid arrest.
Selangor Immigration Department acting director Mohmad Khusairi Kamarudin said the operation focused on businesses suspected of employing foreigners or being operated by them.
"A total of 47 individuals were inspected during the operation.
"Of these, 37 foreigners aged between 18 and 40, including Indonesians, Bangladeshis, Indians and Myanmar nationals, were detained for various immigration offences, including failing to possess valid identification documents and overstaying," he told reporters after the operation.
Khusairi said preliminary checks found that 20 business premises had valid licences, while another 10 were operating without licences.
He said the department had also issued nine witness summonses to Malaysians believed to be the owners of the premises.
He reminded employers against hiring foreigners without valid permits, adding that enforcement action would continue against those who violated immigration laws.
"Our targeted locations are not limited to Klang. Operations will be conducted throughout Selangor," he said.

Title: CapitaLand Malaysia's net profit rises to RM47.02mil in Q3
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: CapitaLand Malaysia Trust's net profit for the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 2026) rose to RM47.02 million from RM34.69 million in the same quarter a year ago.
Revenue increased to RM126.54 million from RM116.04 million previously, with higher revenue from positive rental reversions, rental step-ups at most of its properties and contributions from industrial and logistics assets acquired in 2025, the group said in a Bursa Malaysia filing today.
"Property operating expenses rose marginally by RM200,000, or 0.4 per cent, to RM47.1 million against 3Q 2025.
"This was mainly due to increased utilities expenses, as the automatic fuel adjustment (AFA) tariff changed from a subsidy rate in Q3 2025 to a surcharge rate in the current quarter, and higher provision for doubtful debts," it said.
Its net property income rose by 14.9 per cent to RM79.4 million for the quarter under review versus a year ago.
"Finance cost of RM22.9 million was 7.9 per cent lower than Q3 2025 mainly due to the interest savings arising from medium-term notes refinancing done in Q2 2026 and certain fixed rate loans being refixed at lower rates in first half of 2026," it added.
For the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026 (9M 2026), its net profit rose to RM136.82 million from RM107.24 million, while revenue climbed to RM376.98 million from RM352.14 million previously.
On prospects, it said CapitaLand remains focused on strengthening its portfolio to deliver sustainable income growth and enhance long-term returns amid the current operating environment.
"Targeted asset management initiatives remain a key priority to enhance the value proposition and operating performance of retail properties.
"At the same time, the growing contribution from the industrial and logistics portfolio is expected to further diversify CapitaLand's income streams and strengthen overall portfolio resilience," it said.
CapitaLand will continue to take a disciplined approach to capital allocation, including pursuing value- and yield-accretive acquisition opportunities to support its long-term growth, the filing said.
CapitaLand Malaysia REIT Management Sdn Bhd (CMRM) chief executive officer and CapitaLand manager, Yong Su-Lin said CapitaLand continued to deliver stable performance in Q3 2026, underpinned by healthy demand across its diversified portfolio against a challenging macroeconomic backdrop.
"With a strong balance sheet, we remain well positioned to pursue accretive growth opportunities while continuing to optimise our existing portfolio. We will remain disciplined in our approach to deliver sustainable returns to our unitholders," she said.
CapitaLand is a real estate investment trust (REIT).
As at Sept 30, 2026, CapitaLand's market capitalisation was about RM2.1 billion with total assets of RM5.6 billion.

Title: 59 undocumented foreigners arrested in Penang raids
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: Some 59 undocumented foreigners were arrested in Immigration Department raids at four premises in Bukit Mertajam and Prai.
The Penang Immigration Department said in a Facebook post that 36 people were detained during inspections at a restaurant and an entertainment centre, while another 23 were arrested in separate raids at two factories yesterday.
In the first operation, 55 people were screened, with 35 women and one man arrested.
They comprised 14 Vietnamese, nine Thais, six Indonesians, four Chinese citizens and two Laotians.
In a separate operation under Ops Mahir, 48 people were inspected, with 22 men and one woman detained.
They comprised five Myanmar citizens, five Nepalese, six Chinese citizens, three Sri Lankans, two Bangladeshis and one Indian.
Those detained were suspected of various offences under the Immigration Act, including failing to possess valid travel documents, overstaying and working without valid permits.
The department also took action against an employer for hiring undocumented foreigners at the premises. It did not elaborate.

Title: Indonesian woman arrested over illegal immigration services promoted on TikTok
Article:
SHAH ALAM: An Indonesian woman suspected of using TikTok to promote illegal immigration services, including arranging migrant movements through unauthorised routes, has been arrested following a month-long intelligence operation.
The 31-year-old woman was arrested at a residential premises in Section U15 here on Monday. She is believed to have operated as an illegal immigration agent for about a year.
Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the operation, which began at 10am, was carried out by officers from the department's Intelligence and Special Operations Division at its headquarters in Putrajaya.
"The operation was conducted following information received from the public," he said in a statement.
Zakaria said investigations revealed that the woman had used TikTok to advertise immigration-related services targeting Indonesians living in the Klang Valley.
These included arrangements under the Migrant Repatriation Programme, applications for Special Passes and facilitating migrants' entry and exit through ungazetted routes.
"The suspect was also believed to have offered assistance in obtaining emergency travel documents issued by the Indonesian Embassy.
"She charged between RM700 and RM3,000 for each service offered and is believed to have been operating for approximately a year," he said.
Zakaria said officers seized two Indonesian passports, a set of house keys, two mobile phones, a customer record book and RM4,000 in cash believed to be proceeds from the activities.
"Following questioning, enforcement officers proceeded to a courier company in Puncak Alam, where they seized a parcel containing another Indonesian passport sent by a customer to the suspect," he said.
He said the woman was detained for suspected offences under Sections 56(1)(l) and 56(1A)(a) of the Immigration Act 1959/63, as well as Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963.

Title: More than 20 Bangladeshi passports found at Meru business premises
Article:
KLANG: More than 20 Bangladeshi passports were found at a business premises in Meru here today, prompting an investigation into why the travel documents were being kept there.
The discovery was made during a joint enforcement operation by the Selangor Immigration Department and Klang Royal City Council (MBDK), which began at 11am following intelligence gathering and information received by both agencies.
The operation initially focused on inspecting employers and foreign workers at a row of business premises in the area.
However, enforcement officers discovered a suspicious room at the rear of one of the premises, prompting a more thorough inspection.
Checks uncovered dozens of foreign passports, including several kept in a locked safe.
Selangor acting Immigration director Mohmad Khusairi Kamarudin said more than 20 Bangladeshi passports containing valid particulars were found during the inspection.
"The discovery is suspicious, and the Selangor Immigration Department will conduct further investigations to determine why the passports were being kept at the premises.
"We will also summon the employer, believed to be a Bangladeshi national," he told reporters after the operation.
Meanwhile, a local man in his early 20s who was found looking after the premises claimed he had been paid RM50 by a friend, believed to be a foreigner, to mind the shop for the day.
The premises reportedly sold mobile phones and room furnishings, as well as offering bicycle repair services.
"I was only asked to look after the shop today. He paid me RM50 to stay here until 8pm.
"I don't know who is responsible for the room at the back. Today is my first day working here. I'm serious, I really don't know anything about it," he said.
The Immigration Department is investigating the circumstances surrounding the discovery and seeking to establish who was responsible for keeping the passports at the premises.

Title: Sunway Healthcare, Putrajaya Holdings to build 325-bed hospital
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Healthcare Holdings Bhd and Putrajaya Holdings Sdn Bhd have formalised a 60:40 joint venture to develop a 325-bed multi-specialty private hospital in Putrajaya.
Construction is targeted to begin in the fourth quarter of next year.
The proposed Sunway Medical Centre Putrajaya, which will offer tertiary healthcare and specialist services, is expected to be completed in 2031, subject to the relevant approvals and project timelines.
Their respective wholly-owned subsidiaries Sunway Healthcare Ventures Sdn Bhd and Tapak Senja Sdn Bhd signed the definitive joint venture and shareholders agreement, following a heads of agreement signed on April 23, 2025.
The signing marks Sunway Healthcare's first joint venture hospital project since its listing on the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia in March, advancing the development from planning to its next phase of implementation.
The hospital will occupy about 1.01 hectares of freehold land in Precinct 7, adjacent to Putrajaya Sentral.
It will provide medical services across a broad range of specialties and subspecialties, including a dedicated burns unit.
It is expected to serve residents of Putrajaya, the wider southern Klang Valley and international patients.
This will complement existing healthcare institutions in the administrative capital, including Hospital Putrajaya, Institut Kanser Negara and the Academy of Medicine of Malaysia.
The development is located within Putrajaya's only transit-oriented development, which features Destina Putrajaya, a 97,000 sqft integrated retail destination with pedestrian connectivity to the Express Rail Link (ERL) and MRT stations at Putrajaya Sentral.
Its proximity to rail and road networks, as well as Kuala Lumpur International Airport, is expected to facilitate access for patients from Malaysia and the wider region.
Under the joint venture, Sunway Healthcare will lead the hospital's clinical and operational planning, obtain the necessary operating licences and approvals, and lease and operate the completed facility.
Putrajaya Holdings, as the master developer of Putrajaya, will contribute the land and provide its real estate development and infrastructure expertise to support the hospital's development and integration into the city's wider urban ecosystem.
The partnership combines Sunway Healthcare's experience in developing and operating tertiary and quaternary healthcare facilities with Putrajaya Holdings' expertise in urban development and infrastructure.
Sunway Healthcare Group president Datuk Lau Beng Long said the joint venture marked an important milestone for the group as its first joint venture hospital project since listing.
He said the partnership reflected the group's disciplined approach to expansion and would establish its presence in the nation's administrative capital alongside Putrajaya Holdings, the master developer of Putrajaya.
"With 27 years of operating experience, a network of five hospitals, nearly 2,000 licensed beds, around 80 specialties and subspecialties, and 28 Centres of Excellence, we bring a proven track record in complex and specialised care, clinical excellence, patient experience and hospital operations," he said in a statement.
He noted that both parties aim to develop a hospital that would meet future healthcare needs, broaden access to quality care and strengthen Putrajaya's position as a medical destination for Malaysian and international patients.
