Title: Haze or ship fumes? Maritime experts want closer watch on vessel emissions at Malaysian ports
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Authorities should examine how much ship emissions contribute to air pollution around major ports, particularly during haze episodes originating from Indonesia, says maritime industry expert Datuk Seri Jeyenderan M. Ramasamy.
Jeyenderan, the chief executive officer of Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, said Malaysia’s strategic location along the Strait of Malacca, one of the world’s busiest shipping lanes, offered significant opportunities to develop its marine fuel supply sector, but environmental considerations should not be overlooked.
“As more vessels pass through our waters, we should ensure that ship emissions are properly monitored and that our ports develop sustainably. The environmental impact of shipping activity deserves closer attention, particularly when transboundary haze affects Malaysia,” he said in a statement.
He said Port Klang and ports in Johor were strategically positioned along international shipping routes, giving Malaysia the opportunity to attract more vessels to bunker locally.
However, ships burning heavy fuel oil, including high-sulphur fuel oil (HSFO), can release air pollutants such as sulphur oxides, particulate matter and other combustion-related pollutants, depending on the fuel used and engine operating conditions.
The International Maritime Organization (IMO) introduced a global sulphur limit of 0.50 per cent by mass for fuel used by ships outside designated emission control areas from January 1, 2020.
Ships may use higher-sulphur fuel if they operate under the applicable rules with an approved exhaust gas cleaning system, commonly called a scrubber. The limit for fuel used on board is separate from the rules governing HSFO carried as cargo.
Jeyenderan said the relevant authorities could consider monitoring air quality around major ports, checking compliance with marine fuel sulphur limits and studying pollution levels during haze episodes to better understand the contribution of different sources.
He stressed that reliable monitoring data would help policymakers distinguish between pollution from transboundary haze and emissions from local sources, including shipping, while supporting efforts to balance the maritime industry’s growth with environmental protection.
Echoing the call, Universiti Malaysia Terengganu adjunct professor Nazery Khalid urged the authorities to closely monitor ship emissions during haze episodes, saying Malaysia’s efforts to attract more vessels and expand seaborne trade should not come at the expense of meeting its emissions targets and its international commitments to combat climate change.
“As a responsible maritime nation and a long-standing member of the International Maritime Organization Council, Malaysia is duty-bound to ensure maritime operations in its waters are carried out in an eco-friendly manner, in full adherence to national laws and international standards.
“By ensuring emissions from shipping activities are closely monitored, even during the haze, Malaysia can also underscore its commitment to meeting its net-zero target by 2050. Shipping, which facilitates close to 90 per cent of its trade, and the maritime industry in general can play a leading role in realising this national agenda by operating sustainably,” said Nazery in the joint statement.
He also urged maritime industry stakeholders to take great care to protect the health and well-being of workers, while ensuring activities are not too severely disrupted amid the worsening haze.
“Workers involved in outdoor activities such as shipping, port operations at berthing areas and dockyards, shipbuilding or ship repair, and offshore operations should ensure their health is not compromised while carrying out their tasks,” he said.

Title: Waze ban: MPs ask if WhatsApp, Instagram pose similar security risks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The government has been urged to provide a detailed explanation of the rationale behind the ban on the use of the Waze navigation app by civil servants, as well as the risk levels associated with other popular applications.
Chow Yu Hui (PH-Raub) said that the ban on Waze, over concerns that location data could be exposed to Israel, warranted clarification, particularly regarding how its security risks differed from those of other popular US-owned applications, such as WhatsApp and Instagram.
He said that the United States itself had a record of surveilling foreign leaders and had openly supported Israel, adding that the government should be transparent about the differences in risk levels considered in making the decision.
“The United States has also been implicated in revelations about the surveillance of foreign leaders, including former German Chancellor Angela Merkel. Moreover, the US government supports Israel.
“If Waze is banned on the grounds that its company is based in Israel, when Waze has been owned by Google since 2013, what is the difference in data security risks between Waze and Google Maps, which is owned by the same parent company?” he asked, when debating the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027 at the policy stage in the Dewan Rakyat, today.
Dr Kelvin Yii Lee Wuen (PH-Bandar Kuching) shared similar concerns, raising questions about the security of other applications commonly used by the public.
“It is said that Waze’s database is located in Israel, but many of the applications we use are also controlled by Jewish companies or individuals.
“So, are they also exposed to the same security risks? I am not disputing the possibility of security issues, but I believe a detailed explanation should be provided, because many people are now wondering why this decision was made, and whether they themselves are exposed to these risks,” he said.
Earlier, the government decided to prohibit all civil servants from using the Waze navigation application, to protect government information and users’ personal data from the threat of misuse by the Israeli regime.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the decision took into account the status of Waze Mobile Ltd as a user data controller, incorporated and operating under Israeli law.
The Dewan Rakyat sitting resumes tomorrow. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak announces two months’ salary aid for state civil servants, RM700 for federal staff
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 21 — The Sarawak government today announced a Special Financial Assistance (BKK) equivalent to two months’ salary for state civil servants, as well as a payment of RM700 for federal civil servants serving in Sarawak.
Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg said the two-month salary assistance is based on the last drawn basic salary as of November 2026, with payment scheduled to be made before the end of this year.
“This assistance is expected to benefit 19,851 Sarawak civil servants, with an estimated expenditure of RM144 million,” he said while concluding the debate on the 2027 State Budget at the State Legislative Assembly sitting here today.
For federal civil servants in Sarawak, he announced a one-off payment of RM700.
“This assistance is expected to benefit 132,347 federal civil service personnel, with an estimated expenditure of RM93 million, and will be paid out in the first quarter of 2027.
“For retirees of the Sarawak State Civil Service, we are providing a one-off financial aid of RM500 each to approximately 10,141 recipients, with an estimated expenditure of RM5.1 million,” he said.
Additionally, Abang Johari announced an incentive of RM700 each for private media practitioners registered with six media associations in Sarawak. — Bernama

Title: No casualties after ceiling collapses at Tengku Ampuan Rahimah Hospital’s emergency dept in Klang
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 21 — No patients or hospital staff were involved in a ceiling collapse incident at the Emergency and Trauma Department of Tengku Ampuan Rahimah Hospital (HTAR) in Klang yesterday, the Selangor State Health Department (JKNS) said.
The incident occurred at 7.15pm along the pathway in front of the department’s Blue Zone.
In a statement, JKNS said preliminary investigations found that a leaking pipe in the ceiling had weakened the structure, causing it to collapse.
“Following the incident, safety measures were implemented immediately. The affected pathway was cordoned off, and alternative routes were activated for the movement of patients and staff at HTAR’s Emergency and Trauma Department.
“Cleaning and repair works, as well as a detailed technical investigation, were carried out by the concessionaire to ensure a safe environment,” it said.
JKNS said the repair works had been completed and the pathway reopened at 2.30 am today, with services at the department continuing to operate as usual without disruption.
The department said it remained committed to prioritising the safety of patients, visitors and healthcare workers. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s consumer empowerment index rises to 70.36pc from 63.1pc in 2020
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysian consumers’ empowerment level has improved from moderate to high, with the 2025 Consumer Empowerment Index (CEI) recording an overall score of 70.36 per cent, up from 63.1 per cent in 2020.
Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the increase of 7.26 percentage points reflected consumers’ growing knowledge, confidence and ability to make informed decisions and take action to protect their rights.
“The increase in the score is not merely a statistical figure, but a true reflection of changes in the attitudes and actions of Malaysians as consumers,” he said in a statement today.
He said the Redress Action domain recorded the largest improvement, rising by 10.74 percentage points to 66.84 per cent, indicating that consumers were becoming more capable of lodging complaints and seeking redress when their rights were infringed.
The Purchase Decision domain improved by 7.11 percentage points to 75.91 per cent, while the Financial Literacy domain rose by 3.97 percentage points to 66.47 per cent.
Armizan said the CEI study assessed consumer empowerment across three key areas: financial literacy, purchase decisions, and understanding and exercising the right to seek redress and compensation.
He said the study was first conducted in 2020 to establish a baseline, with the 2025 CEI serving as a follow-up assessment. Benchmarking against the European Union and South Korea was also undertaken to ensure the study’s standards and quality.
Separately, Armizan said the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) would continue to strengthen the Student Consumer Movement (GPS) as a platform for consumer education and advocacy among students at higher education institutions (IPT).
He said 196 GPS clubs had been registered nationwide, with students helping to raise awareness of consumer rights and responsibilities while promoting smart, ethical and responsible consumption.
The 2026 National Student Consumer Movement Assembly, held at the Universiti Pertahanan Nasional Malaysia (UPNM) from Oct 19 to 21, brought together 200 participants from 100 higher education institutions.
Activities included the GPS Exploration Challenge 2026, field visits with KPDN Kuala Lumpur enforcement officers, knowledge-sharing sessions, GPS Idea Lab presentations and the presentation of Food Bank Assistance Grants (i-FB). — Bernama

Title: Selangor ketum raid nets 27 men, including three civil servants
Article:
SUNGAI BULOH, Oct 21 — Three civil servants were among 27 men detained in a raid on a premises believed to be involved in the sale and processing of ketum leaves and water here today.
National Anti-Drug Agency (AADK) deputy director-general (Operations) Zainudin Abdullah said that all the individuals, aged between 19 and 61, were detained in an operation that began at 6am before being taken to the Petaling District AADK Office for documentation.
He said the premises operated daily from noon to midnight and received between 30 and 50 customers a day.
“The value of ketum sold in that location was estimated to be between RM1,000 and RM1,500 per day, with ketum water sold in a small plastic pack for RM10 and in a 1.5-litre bottle for RM20.
“Raw ketum leaves were sold at a price of between RM20 and RM40 per kilogramme (kg), while the raw material was obtained from Kedah at a price of RM12 per kg,” he said to reporters after the raid on the premises today.
Commenting further, Zainudin said the premises also offered cough syrup based on customer requests, which is believed to be used for mixing with ketum water.
He said the seized materials, including ketum leaves and ketum water, will be handed over for further investigation in collaboration with the Sungai Buloh district police headquarters (IPD).
Zainudin said that the operation was part of the Selangor-level Op Perdana, which was conducted simultaneously in six districts in the state from Monday until today to combat the activity.
He said the AADK investigation found that individual involvement in ketum abuse is increasing but following the amendment of the Drug Dependants (Treatment and Rehabilitation) Act 1983, which came into effect in August 2025, the agency is now able to take action against the abuse of the substance.
Meanwhile, an inspection of the premises located on a plot of land near the river found three large pots, each capable of boiling about 20 kg of ketum leaves at a time, while the unboiled ketum leaves were stored in an air-conditioned room to prevent them from wilting.
The premises is also equipped with closed-circuit television (CCTV), in addition to having a small window and a doorbell next to the front door, which are believed to be used for buying and selling transactions. Price tags, phone numbers, and QR codes are also displayed on the wall next to the window. — Bernama

Title: Police arrest male student over alleged axe, penknife attack on teacher at Kuching international school
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 21 — A male Form Four student was arrested after he allegedly attacked a female teacher at an international school here, injuring her this morning.
Sarawak acting police commissioner DCP Saifullizan Ishak confirmed the incident, that occurred at about 8am, adding that a penknife and a small axe were found.
“The police are investigating in detail to ensure the cause of the incident and to obtain evidence.
“Further details about the incident will be made by the Kuching district police chief,” he said in a statement today, adding that the student has been released on police bail.
The case is being investigated under Section 324 of the Penal Code and Section 6(1) of the Explosives Act 1957, he added.
A video showing the student attacking the teacher had gone viral earlier. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia proposes high-level committee with Indonesia to boost creative industry ties
Article:
JAKARTA, Oct 21 — Malaysia has proposed establishing a cross-ministerial High-Level Committee (HLC) with Indonesia to accelerate bilateral cooperation in the creative industries and creative economy.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said that the committee would facilitate discussions on collaborative initiatives, including those that could be formalised through memoranda of understanding (MoUs) with relevant Indonesian ministries.
He said that the proposed mechanism would also help coordinate cooperation across different ministerial portfolios, as areas overseen by Malaysia’s Communications Ministry fell under several ministries in Indonesia, including those responsible for culture, communications and the creative economy.
“The intention is to expedite discussions on matters that would be covered in memoranda of understanding, which will be refined further. As I mentioned earlier, some areas fall under the purview of the Communications Ministry, while others come under several other ministries, as the portfolios are not all the same,” he said.
Fahmi spoke to Bernama after a bilateral meeting with Indonesian Creative Economy Minister Teuku Riefky Harsya here on Wednesday, during which both ministers witnessed the signing of two MoUs between Malaysia's MyCreative Ventures and two Indonesian entities, the Jakarta Creative Economy Committee and EnMasse.
The MoUs were signed by MyCreative Ventures Group chief executive officer Zainol Haqim Zainol Rashid, Jakarta Creative Economy Committee Advisory Board Member Joshua Simandjuntak and EnMasse representative Andi Surya Wirawan Sadha.
Fahmi said the agreements were expected to facilitate closer collaboration and the exchange of creative industry activities between the two countries, particularly in music and related sectors.
On his meeting with Teuku Riefky, Fahmi said he was briefed on the roles and responsibilities of Indonesia’s newly established Creative Economy Ministry under President Prabowo Subianto’s administration, and that they had explored potential areas of cooperation.
“We see many similarities and synergies with the Orange Economy Council that we have established. What is interesting is how they view the various sectors and sub-sectors within the creative economy.
“This will certainly help us examine and assess policy aspects and the implementation of programmes for the creative economy,” he said.
Earlier, Fahmi, who is on a working visit to Jakarta until Thursday, held a separate bilateral meeting with Indonesian Culture Minister Fadli Zon, following discussions with Indonesian Communication and Digital Affairs Minister Meutya Hafid on Tuesday.
Fahmi said his discussions with Fadli focused on strengthening bilateral cooperation, particularly in the film industry.
“We discussed how we could strengthen cooperation, including through an MoU, particularly in the film sector, which we see as having the potential for greater collaboration, including the development of a Nusantara film festival,” he said.
Fahmi said Fadli had also proposed closer cooperation with Malaysia to seek international recognition for Malay cultural heritage, including Jawi script.
“This may not fall under the purview of the Communications Ministry, but we will convey the proposal to the relevant ministries, including the Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry (Motac), regarding the Indonesian Culture Ministry’s intention to nominate Malay heritage, such as Jawi script, for international recognition,” he said.
Fahmi said the proposal could follow the example of the kebaya, which was inscribed on Unesco’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in December 2024 following a joint nomination by Malaysia, Indonesia, Brunei Darussalam, Singapore and Thailand. — Bernama

Title: Langkawi ferry runs aground off Kuala Perlis, all 251 passengers evacuated
Article:
KANGAR, Oct 21 — A total of 251 passengers aboard the Express Bahagia 98 (EB98) ferry from Langkawi, which ran aground on a sandbank near the entrance to the Kuala Perlis Passenger Ferry Terminal this morning, were safely evacuated at 2.50 pm today.
Langkawi Ferry Line Ventures Sdn Bhd Operations Manager Lt Cmdr (R) Norhafiz Abdul Wahid said all passengers, together with their luggage, were successfully evacuated with the assistance of security teams and relevant agencies, while all 10 crew members were also reported safe.
“The evacuation operation was carried out in collaboration with the Kuala Perlis Marine Police, the Kuala Perlis Fishermen’s Association and Sea Splash Travel Sdn Bhd after two initial attempts to tow the ferry using Feri Kenangan 6 and Langkawi Auto Express 1 failed due to the falling sea level,” he said in a statement today.
Norhafiz said the EB98 ferry departed Langkawi at 9.30am before running aground at about 10.35am near Buoy No 1 in Kuala Perlis, when the captain took evasive action to avoid a fishing net stretched across the inbound and outbound shipping channel at Kuala Perlis.
“When the manoeuvre was carried out, both of the ferry’s main engines were stopped before wind conditions caused the vessel to drift onto the sandbank,” he said, adding that efforts to refloat the ferry were scheduled for around 7pm today, when the sea level was expected to rise again.
The operation was planned with the assistance of fishing boats and would depend on tidal conditions and the prevailing circumstances to ensure it could be carried out safely.
Norhafiz said Langkawi Ferry Line Ventures also apologised to passengers and other affected parties for the inconvenience and travel disruptions caused by the incident. — Bernama

Title: More than 3,000 attend Selangor Sultan’s Silver Jubilee royal tea reception in Klang
Article:
KLANG, 21 Oct — The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, graced a Royal Tea Reception with over 3,000 citizens in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee of his reign at Istana Alam Shah here today.
The Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin and the Raja Muda of Selangor, Tengku Amir Shah, were also in attendance.
Their Royal Highnesses were welcomed upon arrival by Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and Selangor State Secretary Datuk Dr Ahmad Fadzli Ahmad Tajuddin.
The Royal Tea Reception, attended by residents from the Hulu Langat, Kuala Langat, Gombak, Sepang and Kuala Selangor districts, is the third of a five-part programme organised in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee of the Sultan of Selangor’s reign.
Meanwhile, Klang District Officer Mohd Hasry Nor Mohd, in his address, pledged the commitment of district-level administrators across Selangor to continue enhancing service quality to be more efficient, transparent, responsive, and principled, for the benefit of the people and the state’s progress.
“The greater responsibility is to ensure that every policy, planning and development implementation truly benefits the people and improves their well-being.
“In executing this trust, His Royal Highness’s decrees and perspectives, particularly concerning governance, integrity, public welfare and state development, serve as an invaluable guide,” he said.
He noted that despite rapid development and increasingly complex social changes, the royal institution will continue to stand as a symbol of stability, unity and continuity for the state.
“Alhamdulillah, under the patronage of His Royal Highness, Selangor continues to flourish as a dynamic, high-potential and competitive state.
“This progress is supported by the wisdom of His Royal Highness’s leadership, the sustained efforts of the state administration, and the support and cooperation of all the people of Selangor,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Kelantan orders data collection on Myanmar refugees across all districts
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 21 — The Kelantan government has instructed all district officers to collect data on the number and locations of Myanmar refugees throughout the state as a preparatory step to address issues related to the community.
State Local Government, Housing, Health and Environment Committee chairman Hilmi Abdullah said that so far, the state government has only received data from the Tanah Merah district, which recorded about 80 families involving more than 300 individuals, in Kampung Padang Guchil, who cultivate betel leaves over an area of two hectares.
He said the village heads were also asked to help conduct a census in their respective villages to obtain information about the community settlement.
“The collection of this data is important to enable the state government to monitor the presence of Myanmar Rohingya refugees, including identifying their settlement areas throughout Kelantan,” he said to reporters after attending the exco meeting at the Kota Darulnaim Complex here today.
Commenting on the jurisdiction of the state government, Hilmi said the state’s powers are limited to matters related to land and premises, including illegal encroachment of government land, violations of private land use conditions, and compliance with business licences under the local authority (PBT).
“If there is encroachment on government land or violation of land conditions, we can take action according to the relevant legal provisions.
“We hope that the issue of Myanmar refugees is not solely placed on the state government, considering our limited jurisdiction in handling that community,” he also said.
Meanwhile, Hilmi added that the state government does not want the settlement of Myanmar refugees to be concentrated in one area, forming a separate colony that could potentially cause problems in the future. — Bernama

Title: Police probe alleged axe attack on teacher by 16-year-old boy at Sarawak international school
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 21 — Police are investigating a 16-year-old male student for allegedly attacking a teacher with an axe at an international school here today.
Acting Sarawak Police Commissioner DCP Saifullizan Ishak said police received a report of the incident at 8.03am via the MERS 999 emergency line.
He said the report alleged that a student had brought firecrackers and used an axe to injure a teacher.
“The victim, a female teacher, reportedly suffered injuries to the hand during the attack.
“The case is being investigated under Section 324 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means, as well as Section 6(1) of the Explosives Act 1957,” he said in a statement.
Saifullizan said police were conducting a detailed investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and gather relevant evidence.
He also urged the public not to speculate or spread unverified information about the case, out of respect for the ongoing investigation and the interests of all parties involved.
The incident has caused concern in Kuching, particularly following reports that the alleged attack was livestreamed on social media.
Footage circulating online purportedly showed the student taking items, including a lighter and an axe, out of a schoolbag while inside a school toilet.
The student appeared to have a mobile phone secured to his head to record the incident, including the moments leading up to the alleged attack.
The footage then became shaky as the student ran towards a classroom, where the attack allegedly took place.
The phone appeared to fall off during the ensuing commotion, causing the livestream to go black, although screams could still be heard in the background. — The Borneo Post

Title: Haze: Schools in KL, Putrajaya and five states to open tomorrow, outdoor activities suspended
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Schools in the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, as well as in Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, Pahang, and Penang, will operate as usual tomorrow; however, all outdoor activities have been postponed due to the haze.
In Kuala Lumpur, the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur Education Department announced that all educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) will conduct in-person classes as usual, even though all outdoor activities are to be postponed.
In Putrajaya, the Federal Territory of Putrajaya Education Department said all schools under its jurisdiction will operate as usual, with students encouraged to wear face masks while at school.
In Selangor, the State Education Department (JPN) announced that all educational institutions under its purview will operate as usual. School administrators are instructed to continuously monitor the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings provided by the Department of Environment and to pay special attention to high-risk students.
In Negeri Sembilan, the State Education Department (JPN) said all MOE educational institutions in the state will operate as usual; however, outdoor activities must be halted if the API reading exceeds 100.
Students are advised to wear face masks particularly those experiencing respiratory symptoms or belonging to high-risk groups while the End-of-Academic-Session Assessments (UASA) scheduled to take place during this period are to be postponed.
In Melaka, the State Education Department (JPN) announced that all educational institutions under its jurisdiction will operate as usual, with all outdoor activities postponed. In the state of Pahang, all schools in the districts of Bentong, Bera, Maran, and Temerloh will operate tomorrow; however, all outdoor activities are suspended.
Meanwhile, the Penang State Education Department has announced that all educational institutions in the state will operate as usual, with schools required to ensure an adequate supply of drinking water for the school community.
Education Departments in the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, as well as in Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, and Penang, are also allowing parents or guardians who are concerned about their children’s health to keep them home from school, provided that the school is notified accordingly.
Yesterday, Minister of Education Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said decisions regarding school closures due to the haze are made collectively by the Ministry of Education (MOE), the Ministry of Health (MOH), and the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES), drawing upon their respective areas of expertise.
She noted that such decisions take into account air quality monitoring and health risks to students, as well as the potential impact on learning should schools remain closed for an extended period. — Bernama

Title: Immigration Dept raids 19 locations in Janda Baik, detains 65 foreigners
Article:
BENTONG, Oct 21 — The Malaysian Immigration Department (JIM) raided 19 locations around Janda Baik in a Mega Integrated Operation this morning and detained 65 foreign nationals for various immigration offences.
Its deputy director-general (Operations), Datuk Lokman Effendi Ramli, said the operation which began at 10am and covered Kampung Cemeruh, Kampung Ceringin and Kampung Sumsum, was conducted following complaints from residents and media reports about the influx of foreign nationals in the resort area.
As a result of the raids on 19 locations including resorts, farms and construction sites, a total of 278 foreign nationals were inspected and 65 of them were detained on grounds for committing offences under the Immigration Act.
"All those detained, aged between 20 and 54 years, will be taken to the Kemayan Depot for investigation and further action," he said at a press conference here today.
He said that among the identified offences were not having a valid pass or permit to be in Malaysia, violating pass conditions, overstaying, using false travel documents, and other offences that violate the Immigration Act.
Lokman Effendi said the integrated operation involved 150 JIM members from Pahang, Kuala Lummpur and the Putrajaya headquarters, in addition to the cooperation of the Road Transport Department (JPJ) and the National Registration Department (JPN).
He also said that in the raid, JIM also issued summons notices to two locals, namely the resort owner and the plantation owner, to appear and give statements as they were suspected of harbouring foreigners.
"On our part, we hope that Malaysians will be more patriotic and not rent out land or business premises to foreigners, as their influx is due to the existence of supply and demand," he added.
Commenting on enforcement nationwide, he informed that JIM has carried out more than 11,000 operations from January 1 until yesterday.
According to him, during that period, nearly 150,000 foreigners were checked, 41,000 were detained, while more than 45,000 were repatriated to their home countries. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia reviews framework for technical aid to developing countries amid global challenges
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysia’s Foreign Ministry is reviewing ways to strengthen the institutional framework for the country’s international development cooperation to better support developing countries grappling with mounting debt, escalating conflicts and the threat of a widening technological divide.
Deputy Foreign Minister Datuk Lukanisman Awang Sauni said the review would draw on insights from a symposium on the Malaysian Technical Cooperation Programme (MTCP), a key instrument of Malaysia’s commitment to developing countries through human capital development, technical assistance and capacity building.
Under the 12th Malaysia Plan (2021-2025), he said the MTCP funded 330 capacity-building programmes benefiting 5,609 participants from 144 developing countries, while supporting 87 scholars pursuing tertiary education in Malaysia.
“Yet, the true impact of MTCP is measured not in numbers, but in outcomes,” he said in his keynote address at the Symposium on MTCP: Prosperity Through Partnership here on Wednesday.
He cited the programme’s support for capacity building in Timor-Leste’s public service ahead of its integration into Asean, a milestone achieved during Malaysia’s Asean chairmanship last year, as an example of its impact.
Lukanisman said the global landscape in which the MTCP operated had grown more complex since the 1980s, with escalating conflicts, mounting debt burdens among developing countries and rapid technological advances threatening to widen the gap between technology creators and consumers.
“Wisma Putra (the Foreign Ministry) is reviewing how best to fortify the institutional framework for Malaysia’s international development cooperation,” he said.
He said Malaysia had reiterated at the United Nations General Assembly last month that the Global South must be empowered as partners in innovation rather than merely treated as clients and markets.
“Technical cooperation is the most practical vehicle to achieve this,” he said.
Also present at the symposium was Acting Director-General of the Institute of Diplomacy and Foreign Relations (IDFR) Datuk Rus Shazila Osman. — Bernama

Title: MCMC records statement of individual over Facebook content allegedly insulting Negeri Sembilan royal institution
Article:
CYBERJAYA, Oct 21 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has recorded the statement of an individual to assist in an investigation into Facebook content suspected of containing elements insulting the Negeri Sembilan royal institution.
In a statement today, MCMC said the action was taken to complete an investigation under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 (Act 588).
“The individual believed to be operating the account appeared at the Cyberjaya Police Station today to assist in the investigation, and one mobile phone and one SIM card were seized,” MCMC said.
MCMC is investigating content uploaded through the Facebook account “Che GuBard”, which is suspected of containing elements insulting the Negeri Sembilan royal institution, as well as touching on the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir and members of the Negeri Sembilan royal family.
MCMC takes seriously any use of online platforms that could incite hatred, insults or disrespect towards the royal institution.
“Freedom of expression must be exercised responsibly and in accordance with the laws of the country. Any further action will be taken based on the findings of the investigation and the applicable legal process,” MCMC said. — Bernama

Title: Home Ministry: Govt has no plans to amend citizenship law for children born before parents’ marriage registration
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The government has no plans to amend Section 17 of Part III of the Second Schedule of the Federal Constitution, which governs the citizenship status of children born before their parents’ marriage is legally registered.
Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Shamsul Anuar Nasarah said the provision remains relevant to ensure that citizenship is determined in accordance with existing laws.
“In view of this, there is currently no proposal to amend Section 17 of Part III of the Second Schedule of the Federal Constitution,” he said during a Special Chamber session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a question from S. Kesavan (PH-Sungai Siput), who asked whether the government would review and amend the provision to prevent children from being denied citizenship solely due to their parents’ marital status.
Elaborating, Shamsul Anuar said being born in Malaysia does not automatically confer citizenship, as the determination depends on marital status and the citizenship status of the biological parents at the time of the child’s birth.
“(This is) in line with the provisions of Part III of the Federal Constitution, the Citizenship Rules 1964 and other relevant laws in force on the registration of marriages, adoption, legitimacy of children and immigration regulations.
“For example, the marriage of non-Muslim couples must be registered under the Law Reform (Marriage and Divorce) Act 1976 (Act 164), while for Muslims, marriage registration is subject to the administration of Islamic religious affairs in their respective states,” he explained.
For children born before their parents’ marriage is legally registered, Shamsul Anuar said the child’s citizenship status is determined by the citizenship status of the biological mother, in line with Section 17 of Part III of the Second Schedule of the Federal Constitution.
However, he said the government does not close the door on individuals who meet the requirements to apply for citizenship through the channels provided by law.
“They may apply, but whether it is approved is subject to the eligibility outlined. Every application must meet the stipulated conditions and be assessed on the entirety of the facts, documents and provisions of the law in force,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Home minister: Malaysia, Japan to strengthen cooperation to combat transnational crime
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysia and Japan are committed to strengthening security cooperation to combat transnational crime through information sharing and investigative collaboration between the Royal Malaysia Police and the National Police Agency (NPA) of Japan.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the matter was discussed during his meeting with Japan’s NPA deputy commissioner-general Tachikawa Koichi here today, on the sidelines of the 20th Asean Ministerial Meeting on Transnational Crime (AMMTC).
He said the discussions focused on expanding information sharing and strengthening investigative cooperation to combat drug trafficking, cybercrime, online scams and human trafficking.
“Transnational crime recognises no national boundaries. Therefore, cooperation among law enforcement agencies is crucial to ensure that preventive, detection and investigative measures can be carried out more effectively,” he posted on Facebook today.
Saifuddin Nasution said Malaysia would continue to strengthen security cooperation with Japan based on trust and mutual respect to safeguard the security and well-being of the people of both countries.
The 20th AMMTC is being held in Manila, the Philippines, with regional cooperation in addressing transnational crime among the key issues under discussion. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak police probe Kuching school incident that left teacher injured
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 21 — Sarawak police are investigating an incident in which a 16-year-old male student allegedly injured a female teacher with an axe at a private school here this morning.
Sarawak acting police commissioner Datuk Saifullizan Ishak said police received information about the incident through the MERS 999 emergency line at about 8.03am today, after the Kuching district police headquarters control centre was alerted to a student allegedly carrying firecrackers and injuring a teacher.
The teacher reportedly sustained cuts to her hand.
In a statement today, Saifullizan said the case was being investigated under Section 324 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt using a weapon and Section 6(1) of the Explosives Act 1957.
He said police were conducting a detailed investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and gather relevant evidence.
Police also urged the public not to speculate or circulate unverified information about the case, in order to respect the investigation and protect the interests of all parties involved.
A video allegedly showing a livestream of the attack has also been widely circulated online.

Title: PMO confirms civil servants barred from using Waze over Israel data security risks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The federal government barred all civil servants from using the Waze navigation application over concerns that sensitive official data and users’ personal information could be harvested and exploited by Israel, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) confirmed today.
In a statement, the PMO confirmed that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim ordered an immediate ban across the public sector to safeguard government data and citizens’ movement information.
“This decision takes into account the status of Waze Mobile Ltd. As the data controller of users, incorporated and operating under Israeli law.
“Sensitive government information and the personal data of the people must be protected from being exploited by the Israeli regime in ways that could compromise national security and sovereignty,” the statement read.
PMO explained that Waze Mobile Ltd, which acts as the legal data controller for all user information collected via the platform, remains incorporated and subject to Israeli jurisdiction.
Official communications stressed that sensitive government logistics and personal travel records must be shielded from state-level exploitation that could compromise national security and sovereign interests.
Anwar also called on the wider Malaysian public to delete the app and migrate to homegrown navigational platforms like TuJu, pointing to the stronger data governance and privacy guarantees provided by domestic solutions.
“The MADANI government’s stance is firm, and we will close any space that can be exploited by the Israeli regime to threaten the security of the nation and its people,” the statement said.
The prohibition formalises a decision reached by the National Cyber Security Committee (JKSN) during its third meeting of 2026 on Oct 20, which was chaired directly by Anwar.
Following the committee’s decision, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar issued a formal circular directing all ministry secretaries-general, federal department heads, state secretaries, statutory body chiefs, and local council leaders to enforce the ban immediately across all departments and subordinate agencies.
Anwar had earlier raised security concerns on Oct 20 regarding the exposure of citizens’ geolocation profiles, pointing out that Waze operates within the Israeli statutory and regulatory framework.
To replace foreign navigation tools, the government is throwing its weight behind TuJu, a local mobility platform jointly developed by the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) and Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd.
Officially unveiled by Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi on Nov 26, 2025, the application is available across major mobile app stores. Alongside turn-by-turn navigation and estimated arrival times, the app integrates real-time highway toll data, live traffic camera feeds, rest-and-service area locator tools, and on-demand highway emergency assistance.

Title: Malaysian Bar, office-bearers awarded RM59,499 after winning part of appeal over 2022 independence march
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 21 —The Court of Appeal today partly allowed the Malaysian Bar’s appeal over its 2022 Walk for Judicial Independence, awarding RM59,499 in damages to the Bar and four of its office-bearers for violating their constitutional rights in connection with the march.
A three-member panel led by Justice Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing ordered the government to pay RM19,499 in special damages to the Bar and RM10,000 each to Karen Cheah Yee Lynn, Mohamad Ezri Abdul Wahab, B. Anand Raj and Murshidah Mustafa, all office-bearers of the Bar when the suit was filed.
The march was held on June 17, 2022, to protest the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s (MACC) public announcement of an investigation into then Court of Appeal judge Datuk Mohd Nazlan Mohd Ghazali, now a Federal Court judge.
The Bar regarded the announcement as interference with judicial independence and a breach of the separation of powers.
On March 20 last year, the Kuala Lumpur High Court held that the police had acted
ultra vires
(beyond their powers) by imposing conditions prohibiting the march, but awarded the Bar only RM1 in nominal damages, a sum proposed by the Bar’s counsel.
The suit was filed on Oct 20, 2022, against six defendants, including former Dang Wangi police chief ACP Noor Dellhan Yahaya, the Inspector-General of Police, the Home Minister and the government, over alleged violations of the plaintiffs’ rights under the Peaceful Assembly Act 2012.
The plaintiffs claimed they were prevented from marching with about 500 members and interns from Padang Merbok to Parliament to submit a memorandum to then prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob or his representative.
Delivering the judgment, Justice Choo, sitting with Justice Datuk Faizah Jamaludin and Justice Datuk Dr Lim Hock Leng, also set aside the High Court’s finding that Kuala Lumpur City Hall’s (DBKL) consent was required for the assembly at Padang Merbok.
The court held that the Bar’s notification to police under Section 9 of the Peaceful Assembly Act 2012 was valid.
“A letter from the Dang Wangi district police chief imposing conditions on the march had been issued out of time and was invalid.
“The Bar had notified police on June 3, 2022, but received the response only on June 16, less than 24 hours before the assembly. Under Section 14 of the Act, police must respond with any conditions within three days,” he said.
However, the bench upheld the High Court’s dismissal of the false imprisonment claim, finding that the participants had not been totally deprived of their liberty.
“While participants were prohibited from marching to Parliament House, they were not physically restrained from leaving the area,” Justice Choo said.
The court also upheld the finding that the police were not liable for misfeasance in public office and dismissed the claim for misconduct in public office, as it failed to meet the high subjective threshold required.
The bench further declined to award general, aggravated and exemplary damages. It ordered interest at five per cent per annum on the sums awarded, from the date of the High Court’s judgment until full settlement, with no order as to costs.
The plaintiffs had sought special damages amounting to RM19,449, general damages and aggravated and exemplary costs, in addition to a declaration that their rights had been violated and a declaration that their detention was illegal and wrongful in law. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar expresses concern over Middle East conflict, condemns Houthi attacks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysia continues to view with great concern the dangerous escalation of conflict unfolding across the Middle East, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar said that he has been in close contact with key regional leaders, including Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Mohammed Salman and Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed Abdulrahman Al Thani.
According to him, these high-level discussions reflect the utmost gravity with which Malaysia regards the crisis and the urgent need to prevent it from widening further.
“Malaysia’s position is clear as we remain steadfast in our call for peace and justice for the Palestinian people, our unequivocal condemnation of the genocide in Gaza and our opposition to the indiscriminate bombing of southern Lebanon,” he said in a post on X today.
He emphasised that this same moral conviction compels Malaysia to speak out with equal firmness whenever innocent civilians are targeted anywhere else.
Consequently, Malaysia reiterates its strong condemnation of attacks by the Houthi movement against civilians and critical civilian infrastructure, such as airports and energy installations in Saudi Arabia and other Gulf Cooperation Council states.
He noted that the recent strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which tragically claimed the lives of innocent civilians, including pilgrims, served as a sobering reminder of the devastating human toll of such violence.
The Prime Minister clarified that Malaysia’s firm stance targets those responsible for the aggression rather than the resilient people of Yemen, who have suffered years of hardship and deserve a lasting political settlement.
Furthermore, he stressed that maintaining the security of the Middle East’s vital sea lanes is paramount for a trading nation like Malaysia.
“Malaysia will continue to support all diplomatic efforts to de-escalate the crisis and safeguard the freedom of navigation,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Johari: Malaysia’s chip talent retention remains sustainable despite foreign offers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Starting salaries for junior engineers and technicians in the local chip industry scale up steadily with experience, offering sustainable career progression even as overseas markets tempt local talent with higher pay, said Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani today.
Addressing questions in Parliament on wage competitiveness and talent retention, Johari said entry-level salaries for junior engineers typically start around RM3,500 and can reach RM6,000 as they gain experience, while technicians can earn between RM3,000 and RM5,000 depending on tenure.
Johari acknowledged the salaries may seem nominally low when compared to what companies in countries like Taiwan or South Korea may offer, but said they must still weigh higher overseas pay against the increased cost of living in those countries.
“If compared with job offers overseas in places like the UK, Singapore, Korea, or Taiwan, salaries might be two to three times higher,” Johari said during Question Time.
“However, the cost of living in those countries will also increase accordingly.”
The Anwar administration is actively trying to position Malaysia as a key chip player by the next one or two decades, rolling out policies it said would help push the domestic semiconductor ecosystem up the value chain.
Southeast Asia’s fourth-largest economy by GDP holds a crucial role in the global transistor supply chain, but only for back-end testing and assembly. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had said he wants Malaysia to shift into front-end design and wafer fabrication.
Retaining skilled human capital through progressive local wage structures remains central to driving the nation’s advanced technology ambitions, but compensation in Malaysia’s industrial sector must be viewed within the context of the domestic standard of living, Johari said.
Still, local pay structures could expand significantly for specialised roles as experience grows, the minister added.

Title: Loke envisions Transport Expo Asia rivalling LIMA as regional mobility showcase
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke hopes the biennial Transport Expo Asia (TXA) will develop into a premier international showcase on par with the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (LIMA), drawing top global exhibitors and industry investors to Malaysia.
Loke said that the event serves as an ideal launchpad to spotlight progress across land transport, aviation, maritime, and logistics sectors, placing particular emphasis on emerging technologies like autonomous driving, robotics, and unmanned aerial systems.
“We want TXA to establish its own brand, much like LIMA, which has become synonymous with Malaysia’s defence industry,” he said during a press conference after witnessing the exchange of memoranda of understanding (MoUs) and bilateral cooperation documents in conjunction with TXA 2026.
Loke pointed out that LIMA, established in the early 1990s, built a formidable global reputation over decades by convening aerospace and maritime manufacturers from around the globe.
He expressed confidence that TXA can chart an identical growth path, anticipating even stronger corporate participation when the exhibition returns for its third edition in 2028.
The trade event has already gained solid traction, recording nearly 5,000 visitors on its opening day yesterday, according to Loke.
The exhibition floor also served as a catalyst for dealmaking, facilitating the formalisation of 17 cooperation pacts aimed at driving sectoral expansion and technology transfer.
“This is something we encourage through Transport Expo Asia, as it provides a platform for industry players to establish strategic partnerships and use the opportunity to formalise their agreements or MoUs.
“We certainly hope this will help drive growth in the transport sector through greater strategic cooperation,” he said.
Rail modernization formed the centrepiece of the commercial exchanges, accounting for 13 of the 17 signed documents, while the remaining four addressed road mobility and maritime operations.
The multilateral pacts bring together government agencies, local operators, tertiary institutions, and overseas strategic partners, advancing Putrajaya’s broader infrastructural modernisation objectives outlined in the National Transport Policy 2030.
Loke said that the Transport Ministry is actively nudging corporations to deepen collaborative research and development with domestic public universities to accelerate the commercial deployment of homegrown inventions.
He cited university-designed vehicular and road safety innovations as tangible proof of how academic-industry links solve real-world mobility challenges.
To nurture youth talent, the exhibition also highlighted tertiary-level innovation initiatives, including a road safety challenge organised in collaboration with energy firm Shell that task university students with creating deployable crash-prevention solutions.
First established in 2025 as the Transport Ministry’s flagship international mobility and logistics exposition, TXA convenes policymakers, venture capitalists, engineering suppliers, and tech developers under one roof. The current three-day showcase runs through Oct 22.

Title: Sarawak completes integrated rare earth elements roadmap to build ‘super magnet’ industry, says Awang Tengah
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 21 — The Sarawak government has completed an integrated framework for the development of the rare earth elements (REE) industry, covering the entire value chain from upstream to downstream activities, said Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Awang Tengah Ali Hasan.
The Second Natural Resources and Urban Development Minister said the Sarawak REE Industry Development Roadmap aims to develop a ‘super magnet’ industry to support the growth of Sarawak’s semiconductor, aerospace, and satellite industries, in addition to applications in electric vehicle manufacturing, defence technology, medicine, and other sectors.
“As an initial step towards developing the industry, the Sarawak government has approved an allocation of RM18 million under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) to conduct studies on the potential presence of REE resources across an area of approximately 3,134 square km.
“In this regard, the federal government has been requested to provide a larger allocation to the Sarawak branch of the Department of Minerals and Geoscience Malaysia to enable the surveys on the presence of these mineral resources to be expanded throughout Sarawak,” he said when winding up his ministerial speech at the State Legislative Assembly (DUN) here.
On a related matter, Awang Tengah said the Sarawak Minerals Management Authority (SMMA) has approved the Sarawak Mineral Industry Development Policy, which comprises seven pillars and 43 key components.
“The policy emphasises the implementation of green mining and quarrying, the use of the latest technologies, human capital development, and the integrated development of the industry across the upstream, midstream, and downstream sectors to increase the value added of products,” he said.
He added that the Green Mining and Quarrying Academy, established through a strategic collaboration between the Centre for Technology Excellence Sarawak and the University of British Columbia (UBC), Canada, will serve as a platform to support the implementation of this policy. — The Borneo Post

Title: KLIA deploys K9 sniffer dog units to tighten airport security and curb smuggling
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 21 — Trained sniffer dog units will begin patrolling passenger terminals and restricted baggage zones across KL International Airport (KLIA) from Oct 26, Malaysia Airports announced today.
The units form a cornerstone of 17 enhanced security measures designed to thwart illicit smuggling and shore up national gateways. The K9 sweeps will operate across three critical operational sectors: the Departure Hall, the Arrival Hall, and the subterranean baggage sorting facilities.
The airport operator described the deployment as a multi-layered security strategy that shields public passenger-facing concourses while reinforcing back-of-house operations alongside existing surveillance architecture.
At check-in and departure gates, the canines will assist handlers in sniffing out prohibited substances and identifying security threats tied to high-risk flight profiles. In Customs inspection corridors, the dogs will intercept undeclared contraband, narcotics, and smuggled commercial goods.
Down in the baggage sortation areas, K9 units will inspect checked luggage before ramp crews load bags onto departing aircraft or transfer incoming cargo to passenger reclaim belts. To maintain animal welfare between rigorous operational shifts, dedicated rest stations and handler amenities have been designated across both terminals.
Malaysia Airports managing director Datuk Mohd Izani Ghani said integrating canine units into daily operations strengthens inter-agency vigilance to safeguard international travellers, visitors, and airport staff, while freeing airport Aviation Security (AVSEC) teams to concentrate on their primary protective functions.
“This collaboration also allows our Aviation Security personnel to remain focused on their core responsibility of safeguarding airport users and facilities.
“We will continue to support the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency, the Royal Malaysia Police, Royal Malaysian Customs Department and the K9 units in ensuring that KLIA remains a safe, comfortable and clean airport for everyone,” Mohd Izani said.
An initial pilot phase will fine-tune terminal standard operating procedures, secure restricted-area access protocols for handlers and dogs, and adjust patrol intervals to prevent disruptions to peak passenger movements.
The enhanced security perimeter arrives amid intense public scrutiny following several brazen narcotics trafficking cases traced back to Malaysian departure gates in recent months, though Malaysia Airports did not tie the canine rollout to any specific incident.
The deployment follows recent drug arrests abroad involving Malaysians said to have departed from KLIA.
On Oct 10, Japanese customs enforcement detained five young Malaysians aged 19 to 26 upon their arrival at Tokyo's Haneda International Airport after officers discovered five kilograms of cocaine hidden inside the hollowed-out soles of their platform shoes. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan confirmed on Oct 16 that the syndicate couriers, including a married couple travelling under the guise of tourists without prior criminal records, boarded their flight from KLIA Terminal 2.
The Haneda seizure followed an earlier scandal in July, when a 39-year-old Malaysian commercial airline pilot was intercepted at Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Jakarta in possession of 25 kilograms of ecstasy and methamphetamine pills valued at an estimated RM45 million.

Title: No more ‘kindergarten colours’: DBKL opts for neutral tones in RM446m public housing facelift
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The capital’s public housing schemes are receiving a major aesthetic and safety facelift, with City Hall (DBKL) foregoing garish paint schemes for neutral tones while overhauling critical electrical infrastructure across dozens of ageing buildings.
Speaking during a working visit to People’s Housing Programme (PPR) Taman Mulia in Bandar Tun Razak today, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said that DBKL made a deliberate shift away from the bright, multi-coloured exteriors long associated with government flats.
Accompanying her on the site inspection were Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud and Bandar Tun Razak MP Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail.
“I would like to add that the colours chosen by DBKL are neutral colours, for the residents to know that this is a residential area and not a kindergarten.
“Many PPRs have been colourful, so we have chosen neutral colours,” she said.
Aside from the cosmetic exterior refresh, Yeoh said that the priority remains addressing life-threatening structural risks.
DBKL partnered with the Institution of Engineers Malaysia to conduct comprehensive technical audits across public housing schemes and municipal flats citywide, targeting deteriorating electrical risers and wiring to avert catastrophic fire hazards.
At PPR Taman Mulia, DBKL committed RM6.67 million in restorative works for roughly 2,128 residents. The project includes RM3.48 million towards repainting the towers, RM2.55 million to replace sub-main cabling and main switchboards, RM370,000 for internal road resurfacing, and RM272,000 to modernize fire prevention systems.
Mayor Fadlun said the citywide rehabilitation drive is moving steadily, with around 70 per cent of targeted projects completed. DBKL set 64 public housing sites for refurbishment in 2026, aiming to cross the 80 per cent completion line before year-end.
“The rest has been allocated for the 2027 budget, which we will continue for the PPRs and PAs that are not ready,” he said.
Fadlun further noted that Putrajaya has earmarked RM446 million in total for upgrading works across public housing estates and municipal flats, tailoring allocations to the specific infrastructural deficits of each scheme.
To ensure financial governance, DBKL plans to erect transparency signboards at individual housing estates displaying line-item expenditure, giving residents a clear accounting of public funds spent on their blocks.
Dr Wan Azizah reminded the community that structural improvements require civic responsibility, urging residents to safeguard shared amenities and combat vandalism.
“I see improvements, mainly in the PPRs area. However, what I would like to suggest is to take care of the infrastructure,” she said, noting that upkeep is indispensable if families are to enjoy secure and dignified living quarters.
Built in 2002, PPR Taman Mulia houses 912 residential units across two 21-storey towers. Having clocked more than two decades of heavy wear and tear, key mechanical and electrical fixtures required substantial rehabilitation to maintain habitability standards.
The estate was handed over to its Joint Management Body (JMB) on Dec 1, 2025, alongside a professional management agent to handle day-to-day estate administration.
DBKL reiterated that preserving public housing standards depends on continuous cooperation between the municipality, building managers, and resident committees.

Title: Malaysians who lend MyKad to foreigners face up to three years’ jail, says Home Ministry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Individuals who misuse their identity cards (MyKad) by ‘renting out’ or handing them over to foreign nationals could face up to three years in prison, a fine of up to RM20,000, or both, Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Dr Shamsul Anuar Nasarah said.
He said the National Registration Regulations 1990 provide strict legal measures to curb foreign nationals’ misuse of national identity.
“The government takes this matter seriously, with enforcement aimed not only at penalising offenders but also at preventing identity misuse and identifying such cases at an early stage,” he said during a question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was replying to a supplementary question from Mohamad Shafizan Kepli (GPS-Batang Lupar) about reports of some Malaysians renting out their MyKad to foreign nationals for only RM100 to work in factories.
Mohamad Shafizan had earlier highlighted the detention of 36 foreign factory workers in Pasir Gudang during Ops Jejak 1.0 yesterday for allegedly using fake MyKad or those belonging to other people to gain employment.
Shamsul Anuar said the operation underscored the importance of joint enforcement efforts by the National Registration Department (NRD), the Immigration Department and Labour Department.
“The operation also focused on the possible involvement of original identity card holders suspected of renting out or handing over their documents to foreign nationals for employment purposes,” he said.
On enforcement efforts, he said the NRD had carried out 4,174 operations nationwide from 2022 to September this year, resulting in 1,868 arrests.
He said 577 cases were prosecuted under Regulation 25(1)(e) of the National Registration Regulations 1990 during the same period, comprising 449 cases involving the use of fake MyKad and 128 involving the use of others’ identity cards. — Bernama

Title: Teacher injured while disarming student in Kuching school
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 21 — A teacher was injured while attempting to wrest a sharp object from a student at an international school here this morning.
It is learned that the secondary school student was brought under control and taken to the principal’s office before the police arrived and took over the matter.
The teacher was taken to the hospital for treatment.
Kuching district police chief ACP Alexson Naga Chabu, when contacted, said the police are looking into the incident.
There was no immediate information on what further action was taken on the student.
Efforts to contact the school for comments were unsuccessful.
An email purportedly sent by the school to its staff and parents of students, said the incident was isolated and no other injuries were reported.
It also said the students of the school were not in danger throughout the incident as they had been promptly moved to safety as precaution.
Lessons were ended early to allow police investigations. — The Borneo Post

Title: Find another way: Civil servants effectively banned from using Waze app due to Israel ties
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Civil servants have been banned from using the Waze navigation app with immediate effect, following a decision by the National Cyber Security Committee (JKSN) at its meeting yesterday.
In a letter dated October 20, Chief Secretary to the Government (KSN) Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar said the JKSN Meeting No. 3 of 2026 was chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Shamsul Azri said all secretaries-general and department heads must ensure the decision is communicated to officers under their supervision, including related agencies and departments, for immediate implementation.
“Any queries or requests for further clarification regarding this directive may be submitted to the National Cyber Security Agency (NACSA), National Security Council, Prime Minister’s Department, as the coordinating agency for this matter,” the letter read.
He also sought cooperation and serious attention to ensure the decision is fully complied with at the ministry, department and agency levels.
The letter was addressed to all ministry secretaries-general, heads of federal departments, heads of management of federal statutory bodies, state government secretaries and heads of management of local authorities.
Yesterday, the Prime Minister encouraged the public to use the local TuJu app, developed by the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM), as an alternative for road navigation.
Anwar said the recommendation followed security risks to users’ information and movement data from using Waze, which is bound under Israeli government laws.
TuJu was developed by LLM in collaboration with Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd and launched by Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi on Nov 26, 2025.
The app, available on the Google Play Store and Apple App Store, provides route information, travel distance, estimated time of arrival (ETA), toll and real-time traffic information, as well as rest and service area (R&R) facilities, live CCTV access and emergency assistance. — Bernama
